title: Feature Switches Build Plan
eyebrow: Build plan for approval · feature switches (#535) · three steps, nothing built yet

short.lead: You approved the feature switches with choices 1A, 2A and 3A. Here is how they get built: three steps, one issue each (#536, #537 and #538), on the branch AjsAgent/phase-3-handoff with the rest of phase 3, and tested in phase 3's QA. The hook script hook.py already reads its input first. One new call right after that read sets every existing HOUSE_RULES_ setting for that prompt. Every check then obeys the switches without being edited. Only the rule for writing pages needs a new setting, because today it is switched together with the design loop. You have no new choices to make on this page.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it changes.
items: #536: a switch you type in any folder is saved for that folder, or for the whole machine if you add "everywhere". Once the hook has read its input, one call turns each switch group into the HOUSE_RULES_ settings it covers.

#537: a new HOUSE_RULES_PAGES setting. Off means three things stop: the page-writing rule, the rule that a reply of 160 words or more needs a page, and the editor pass on pages. Approvals still move the feature to its next stage.
#538: the note on each prompt says which groups are off and where each was set. Switched-off rule text is left out of the session, and /house-rules:mode lists every group.
Tested as the rest of phase 3
Each step's cases fail before the change and pass after; the full verify.py passes. A live headless session in a folder that is not a git repository shows "pages off" working.

changes: chg
Step 1: Saved anywhere, applied everywhere (#536)
No folder, git or not, is stuck with every feature on.
Two switches, git repositories only
Seven groups plus a master switch, in any folder or machine-wide

In core.py, the function _mode_file now finds a switch file outside git folders too. A line ending in "everywhere" writes the copy in the Claude config folder. A small table maps each group to its settings. The new call in hook.py, right after core.keep_payload(), applies them. A folder's switch beats a machine-wide one, and a machine-wide one beats settings.json. The guards and the credit check belong to no group, so they stay on.
chg
Step 2: Pages on their own (#537)
You can keep approvals and drop pages.
Pages switch only with the whole design loop
HOUSE_RULES_PAGES turns the page rule off alone
handover_page_row, the 160-word rule and the page editor check read the new setting as well as the loop's.
chg
Step 3: What you see (#538)
You always know what is off and why.
The note names only two switches
Every off group, and where it was set
The prompt note (_mode_note in the code) and the filter that leaves out switched-off rule text now know the new groups. The command /house-rules:mode prints a table of all the groups.
new
How it is tested
The same checks as the rest of phase 3.
Cases written to fail first, the full verify.py, one live headless session outside git, and your QA.
